h2: NDT training near Minneapolis–St. Paul: Ridgewater College, trainee jobs and online theory with an on-site practical compared

NDT training near Minneapolis–St. Paul: Ridgewater College, trainee jobs and online theory with an on-site practical compared

Twin Cities candidates have something many metros lack: a full college NDT program within about an hour's drive. Ridgewater College teaches NDT at its Hutchinson campus west of the metro, and inspection companies in the Twin Cities hire assistants who learn on the job. Between the two sits a third route, self-paced theory online with the practical done at your employer.

Who offers NDT training around Minneapolis?

  • Ridgewater College, Hutchinson. An in-person program with an associate of applied science (60 credits), diplomas of 45 or 60 credits and 16-credit certificates. Named awards include an NDT AAS, an NDT diploma, a Welding and NDT Methods diploma, a Radiographic Testing certificate and an Ultrasonic Testing certificate. Students work hands-on in X-ray and isotope radiography, ultrasonics, eddy current, magnetic particle and penetrant, with lab hours Monday to Thursday and full- or part-time study.
  • Assistant jobs with inspection companies. Acuren has advertised NDT/RT assistant roles in St. Louis Park: setting up equipment, helping radiographers with calibration and tests, and recording results. The posting asked for supporting QA documents proving classroom hours, a background check so the hire can be certified as "Trustworthy & Reliable", and a driving record that meets company standards.
  • Plant and manufacturer training. Refineries, aerospace and medical-device makers and food-grade equipment fabricators train their own staff under written practices.
  • ASNT Minnesota Section. Listed by ASNT, and the place to meet Level IIIs and hiring managers from across the state.

Proof of classroom hours matters here

That St. Louis Park requirement is worth noticing: even an assistant role wanted documented classroom hours before day one. A training record that lists the method, topics and hours is therefore useful before you are hired, not only when you sit a Level II exam. Whichever provider you use, keep the record, make sure it is signed, and ask the employer whether it meets their requirement.

Ridgewater or online theory?

They serve different people. Ridgewater gives a newcomer supervised lab time across several methods and a college award, at the cost of regular attendance in Hutchinson; its Welding and NDT Methods diploma is aimed at someone who wants both skills. Online theory suits a person who is already employed, or has an assistant job lined up, and needs a single method documented without leaving work. A Ridgewater graduate can still use online study later to add a method, and an assistant can use it to build the classroom hours that the next level asks for.

Which route fits you?

Where you areTwin Cities routeRemember
No NDT background, free to study for a year or moreRidgewater's diploma or AASIn person, in Hutchinson
Want to start work quicklyClassroom hours online, then an assistant roleLog every supervised hour
Working technician adding a method or levelOnline theory, then the practical and exams with your employerConfirm credit for outside hours
Employer certifying a crewOn-site training and Level III exam administrationFinish before the busy outage season

Questions for any Twin Cities NDT training provider

  • Will the record show hours by method in a form employers recognize?
  • Which levels does each course prepare you for?
  • Who administers the practical exam?
  • Is a Level III reachable during the course?

Where Atlantis fits for Minneapolis candidates and employers

Atlantis method theory is online and self-paced, so it gives you a documented record of formal training hours to show an employer without a commute to Hutchinson. An ASNT Level III answers questions, and access opens as soon as you enroll. You practice set-ups in the Practical NDT simulator; the hands-on practical and practical exam follow at your employer's facility under a written practice built on SNT-TC-1A, and certification is your employer's decision. Begin with NDT Level 1 training, then NDT Level 2 training in the methods your target employer uses, often UT and MT.

Twin Cities refiners, fabricators and inspection contractors that certify technicians in-house can bring the training to their own plant, have a Level III review the written practice and run the general, specific and practical exams, and keep a certification file that stands up when a customer audits it.

Work out the hours you need with the SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker. Weld inspectors can see CWI exam prep for Minneapolis, and neighboring pages cover Minnesota, Milwaukee and Des Moines.
